bottleneck: Adult mammalian spinal axons do not regenerate: inhibitory myelin proteins (Nogo, MAG, OMgp), the glial scar's chemical and physical barrier, and an intrinsic loss of neuronal growth programs block repair after injury. Partial approaches — scar digestion with chondroitinase, growth-factor delivery, stem cell grafts — each address one barrier while the others persist, and regrowing axons must navigate a disrupted landscape to find correct targets. Complete injuries remain functionally permanent despite decades of research, because regeneration is a systems problem being attacked one target at a time.
current_state: Epidural stimulation plus rehabilitation restores some function in trials by engaging spared circuits, but true axonal regeneration across a lesion has not been achieved in humans.

sources.title: Brain Connectome: Mapping Neural Networks in Neuroscience

title: Spinal axons cannot regenerate past the lesion
why_it_blocks: Paralysis is permanent because multiple repair blockers act in concert and no therapy defeats them simultaneously. Until regeneration is solved as a systems problem, spinal cord injury stays irreversible.
